name: compare-review
title: Compare Review
description: The whole diff-review surface — history rail, two version panes, a properties/code rail, and side-by-side or overlay. Headless: the host supplies the modal and both renderers.

files.content:
"use client" import { useCallback, useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react" import { AlertTriangle, PanelBottom, PanelRight } from "lucide-react" import { cn } from "../lib/utils" import { Button } from "./button" import type { BoardCompare, CompareChange } from "./compareModel" import { CodeView } from "./codeView" import { HistoryList, type HistoryRecord } from "./historyList" import { PropertyTable, type ElementReview, type TableLayout } from "./propertyTable" import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "./tabs" import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from "./toggle-group" /** * src/components/compareReview.tsx — the headless Compare dialog BODY * (docs/menus/screenshots/08-compare-changes.png): the HISTORY rail, the * two centre panes, the right/bottom detail rail (Properties|Code over * lane K's `PropertyTable`/`CodeView`), and the bottom * Side-by-side|Overlay + Fullscreen bar. No `Dialog`, no fixed * positioning, no z-index EXCEPT overlay's own stacking (the two panes share one * grid cell, so the after pane is raised above the before pane and the * combined caption above both — all contained by `isolate` on the stage, so * none of it reaches the host's stack) — MENU-KIT-DESIGN.md §3.3 is explicit that "a * thin host modal wraps it." * * Ported structurally (JSX shape, not the math — there is none here) from * /home/bam/systemsketch/src/compare/CompareDialog.tsx, with everything * the design doc's host contract (§4, "Compare:") assigns to the host cut * away: `Dialog.Root/Portal/Overlay/Content` (:660-679, :1120-1126) and the * `.systemsketch-theme-root` portal target — a host wraps this in * whatever modal/portal primitive it already owns; the ThemeRoot query the * donor used to find that portal target is replaced everywhere in this * kit by the universal `container` prop (design doc §4). Snapshot/version * discovery, `recordsOfSnapshot`, and `BoardRender`'s camera linking * (:354-397) are also host-side — `renderBefore`/`renderAfter` below take * their place as plain render-prop slots, per this lane's brief ("both * centre panes take a host-supplied ReactNode renderer — this component * knows nothing about boards"). * * - History rail: donor :721-773 (`aside.systemsketch-compare__history`). * The `source` early-return (:729-745, "no file history to page * through") is `sourceNote` here; the ordinary path (:747-772) mounts * the SAME `HistoryList` this kit's Block inspector uses, per that * component's own WHY ("you only have to understand the interaction * pattern once"). * - Centre panes + bottom bar: donor :776-890 * (`.systemsketch-compare__stage`/`__panes`/`__stagebar`). The * donor's FULLSCREEN bar contents (:822-847 — a version stepper and a * "Return to modal" swap) are cut: `MENU-KIT-DESIGN.md`'s host * contract puts "fullscreen promotion" on the host ("kit emits * `data-fullscreen` and `onStageShapeChange`; host restyles and * re-frames"), and a version-stepper widget is no more this lane's * write set than `BoardRender` is. `fullscreen` still flips the same * boolean and stamps the same `data-fullscreen` attribute the donor * read to branch (:679); a host that wants the donor's fuller * immersive chrome swap is free to render around this component * differently in that state; hiding this component's own rail/detail * underneath it is exactly what `data-fullscreen` on the root is for. * - Detail rail: donor :892-1030 (`aside.systemsketch-compare__detail`). * The tab strip's `nav.block-inspector__tabs` (:894-921) is this * kit's own `tabs.tsx` instead, per that file's header note and the * donor's own words quoted there ("Very important that we are * consistent with what tabs look like"). The dock-toggle button * (:945-961) keeps its exact WHY (icon shows the DESTINATION, not the * current state — "Dock to the bottom" is actionable, "Docked right" * is a status nobody asked for) and its exact placement (riding the * tab strip, not the bottom bar — "a control that moves a panel * belongs ON that panel"), but the donor's hand-drawn `DockIcon` SVG * (:1095-1114) is replaced by lucide's `PanelBottom`/`PanelRight` — * both already read as "a frame with one edge filled", which is the * donor's own description of what it drew, and this kit's stock-part * rule for icons (MENU-KIT-DESIGN.md §5, "Icons in menus/bars") is * "lucide-react named exports", not a hand-drawn one-off. The amber * `problem` notice (:924-928, ink text on a tinted left-bar rather * than colored text on a colored fill) copies `draftBar.tsx`'s * `ConflictBanner` pattern verbatim rather than reinventing a second * warning treatment — same measured sub-AA-contrast reason, same * literal `amber-*` swatches (no `--warning` token exists yet). * - Action/review footer: donor :1032-1085 * (`footer.systemsketch-compare__actionbar`). `action`/`review` are * unchanged data shapes; the busy/error state machine the donor kept * on the dialog component itself (`actionBusy`/`actionError`, not * shown in this excerpt's line range but read by :1033-1085) is kept * here for the same reason — `action.onConfirm()` is an async host * call and something has to own "in flight" while it resolves. * * `onStageShapeChange` reproduces the donor's own `stageShape` stamp * (:386, `` `${fullscreen}:${dock}` ``) verbatim — the WHY the design doc * keeps it for ("replaces the 140/420ms timers") is the donor's own * comment at :376-397: re-framing on a CSS Grid template change needs to * fire once the LAYOUT has actually settled into its new shape, not on a * timer tuned to how long that used to take on one machine. */ export type CompareMode = "side-by-side" | "overlay" export type CompareTab = "properties" | "code" export type CompareDock = "right" | "bottom" /** What an action reported when the reviewer confirmed it. */ export interface CompareActionOutcome { readonly ok: boolean /** Why it was refused. Shown in the action bar; the dialog stays open. */ readonly reason?: string } /** Turns the review into a REVIEW-AND-APPLY (Merge, Rebase). Absent → a plain review: no checkboxes, no bottom bar. */ export interface CompareReviewAction { /** The verb. Names the confirm in fallbacks. */ readonly label: string /** The confirm button's text, given how many changes are on screen — a caller has to handle 0 itself. */ confirmLabel(changeCount: number): string /** Run the REAL action — never a re-derivation from what this view is showing. */ onConfirm(): Promise /** Set when there is nothing safe to apply (e.g. a conflicted rebase). The confirm disables; this says why. */ readonly blockedReason?: string } /** The accept/reject affordance's data, present only in review-and-apply mode. */ export interface CompareReviewSelection { readonly rejectedIds: ReadonlySet onToggleReject(id: string): void /** Overrides the default "re-check N unchecked elements" sentence. */ noteFor?(rejectedCount: number): string } export interface CompareReviewProps { comparison: BoardCompare | null versions?: readonly HistoryRecord[] selectedVersionId?: string | null onSelectVersion?(id: string): void /** An explicit before/after pair with no file history to page through — replaces the version rail with a "Comparing X vs Y" note. */ sourceNote?: { beforeLabel: string; afterLabel: string } /** The amber notice, as data — e.g. "No prior versions found beside this board." */ problem?: string | null renderBefore(slot: { highlight: CompareChange | null; label: string }): ReactNode renderAfter(slot: { highlight: CompareChange | null; label: string }): ReactNode selectedChangeId: string | null onSelectChange(id: string | null): void /** * Which element the Figma-layout property table opens expanded. * * WHY this became a prop: the comment below still holds for a LIVE review * — nothing outside the table cares which element is expanded mid-session * — but "nothing cares" and "nobody can set it" are different claims, and * only the first was true. Setting `selectedChangeId` does not select an * element (they are separate concerns), so there was no way to open this * surface with a row already showing: a host restoring a review session * could not, and the stories' own `AllStates` gallery captioned two cells * "Element selected" and "Properties tab — the table…" while both rendered * "Select an edited element to compare changes" with no table at all. An * independent judge opened the gallery and read the empty state back * (2026-09-18). * * Uncontrolled-with-a-default rather than fully controlled, deliberately: * the expanded row genuinely is view-local once the surface is open, so a * host should not have to own it turn by turn — it only needs to be able * to say where to start. */ defaultSelectedElementId?: string | null /** Host cameras. Fired whenever the selected change (and therefore what should be framed) changes. */ onFrameChange?(change: CompareChange | null): void mode: CompareMode onModeChange(mode: CompareMode): void blend: number onBlendChange(pct: number): void /** Overlay only means anything with linked cameras — gates the Overlay option when the host can't link them. */ canOverlay?: boolean /** Host promotes; this component only stamps `data-fullscreen` and flips the bar's own controls. */ fullscreen: boolean onFullscreenChange(next: boolean): void onStageShapeChange?(shape: string): void dock: CompareDock onDockChange(dock: CompareDock): void tab: CompareTab onTabChange(tab: CompareTab): void /** Initial values — this component owns the live state from here, the same way `propertyTable.tsx`'s header note describes ("the host — `compareReview.tsx` — still owns the state"). See the file-level decision note below `CompareReview`. */ layout: TableLayout gitHighlight: boolean action?: CompareReviewAction review?: CompareReviewSelection /** Portal target for a future popup-bearing child. Nothing in this surface portals today; accepted for host-contract completeness (§4, "Universal"). */ container?: HTMLElement | null testIdPrefix?: string } export function CompareReview({ comparison, versions, selectedVersionId = null, onSelectVersion, sourceNote, problem, renderBefore, renderAfter, selectedChangeId, defaultSelectedElementId = null, onSelectChange, onFrameChange, mode, onModeChange, blend, onBlendChange, canOverlay, fullscreen, onFullscreenChange, onStageShapeChange, dock, onDockChange, tab, onTabChange, layout, gitHighlight, action, review, testIdPrefix, }: CompareReviewProps) { const prefix = testIdPrefix ?? "compare" const versionList = versions ?? [] /* * DECISION (not fully spelled out by MENU-KIT-DESIGN.md §3.3's props * sketch, which lists `layout`/`gitHighlight` with no setter — see * `propertyTable.tsx`'s own header note: "the host (`compareReview.tsx`) * still owns the state"): `PropertyTable` is a controlled component that * REQUIRES `onLayoutChange`/`onGitHighlightChange` to do anything at * all, so something has to hold that state. Treating the two props as * SEED values for local state here — rather than either (a) silently * adding the two missing callbacks to this component's own public * props, which the design doc's sketch does not ask for, or (b) making * the toggle/checkbox permanently inert — is what lets a host configure * an initial layout without this component reaching back up for * something nothing above it actually needs to know. */ const [layoutState, setLayoutState] = useState(layout) const [gitHighlightState, setGitHighlightState] = useState(gitHighlight) // Figma-layout's own element selection is view-local once the surface is // open; `defaultSelectedElementId` only decides where it STARTS. See that // prop's own WHY for why the distinction mattered. const [selectedElementId, setSelectedElementId] = useState(defaultSelectedElementId ?? null) const [actionBusy, setActionBusy] = useState(false) const [actionError, setActionError] = useState(null) const selectedChange = comparison?.changes.find((change) => change.id === selectedChangeId) ?? null const handleSelectChange = useCallback( (id: string | null) => { onSelectChange(id) onFrameChange?.(id ? (comparison?.changes.find((change) => change.id === id) ?? null) : null) }, [onSelectChange, onFrameChange, comparison], ) // Ported verbatim (donor :386): a stamp on the two things that decide // this surface's actual on-screen shape, fired once so a host can // re-measure/re-frame after the CSS grid actually settles — never on a // timer. const stageShape = `${fullscreen}:${dock}` useEffect(() => { onStageShapeChange?.(stageShape) }, [stageShape, onStageShapeChange]) const runAction = useCallback(async () => { if (!action) return setActionBusy(true) setActionError(null) const outcome = await action.onConfirm() setActionBusy(false) if (!outcome.ok) setActionError(outcome.reason ?? "Could not apply the change.") }, [action]) const reviewAdapter: ElementReview | undefined = review ? { isAccepted: (elementId) => !review.rejectedIds.has(elementId), onToggle: (elementId) => review.onToggleReject(elementId), } : undefined const beforeEntry = versionList.find((record) => record.id === selectedVersionId) ?? null const beforeLabel = sourceNote ? sourceNote.beforeLabel : (beforeEntry?.title ?? "Previous version") const afterLabel = sourceNote ? sourceNote.afterLabel : "Current version" const changeCount = comparison?.total ?? 0 const rejectedCount = review?.rejectedIds.size ?? 0 const canConfirm = Boolean(action) && !action?.blockedReason && !actionBusy && rejectedCount === 0 const historyRail = (
